claim: Ultra-processed foods — industrially formulated products built from refined ingredients and additives, often engineered into 'hyper-palatable' combinations — made up about 67% of the calories consumed by U.S. youths aged 2 to 19 by 2018, up from about 61% in 1999, according to a 2021 analysis in JAMA of national nutrition-survey data.

sources.label: Wang L, et al., 'Trends in Consumption of Ultraprocessed Foods Among US Youths Aged 2-19 Years, 1999-2018,' JAMA (2021)
sources.quote: From 1999 to 2018, the estimated percentage of total energy from consumption of ultraprocessed foods increased from 61.4% to 67.0%

sources.label: Cole Soiney / @rant.board, Instagram reel DZJJvUbtJ2g (June 3, 2026) — surfacing source

notes: Exact figures from the JAMA (Journal of the American Medical Association) abstract: 61.4% (1999) to 67.0% (2018) of total energy intake among US youths aged 2-19; n=33,795; NHANES data. The reel's '67% of kids' calories today' matches the 2018 endpoint. 'Ultra-processed' follows the NOVA classification. JAMA full-text may sit behind an access wall — quote verified against the published abstract.
